notes.decision: Rendered tentatively as 'the abode.' The lexeme ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ̈ is unusual; possible underlying forms include ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ ('honor'), a derivative of ⲭⲱ ('place, set, abide' — qualitative ⲭⲏ), or even Greek τύχη. The following clause ('the tabernacle is established in him') strongly supports a dwelling/abode-sense, since the second cosmic chariot must be a locus capable of housing the σκηνή. Confidence low.

Translated 'shone forth' — taking ⲡⲓⲉ as a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲓⲣⲉ/ⲡⲣⲓⲉ ('to shine forth, radiate'), the same root as ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' established in vocabulary. Fits perfectly with the following sequence: shone-forth → came down → manifested in the world.
Translated as 'the Call' and 'the Answer' — the canonical Manichaean pair (German Ruf/Antwort). ⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ = 'invitation/calling,' ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ = 'hearing/response.' Capitalized as cosmic hypostases.
Parsed as ϫⲓ-ⲧⲱϩⲥ 'receive anointing' (ⲭ for ϫ in Lycopolitan). The Manichaean apostle is anointed in/by the living Air.
Read as the Lycopolitan ordinal 'the ninth' (= ⲯⲓⲥ/ⲯⲓⲧⲉ). Position in the enumeration (between eighth and tenth) confirms.
Translated 'is mingled' — taking as ⲉⲧⲏⲡ (qualitative of ⲱⲡ 'count/reckon/mix') with doubled ⲡ. The living Fire is the principle reckoned/mingled within all the other elements.
Rendered 'forms' — taking as ϩⲣⲃ 'form, semblance, figure' (Crum 700a).

Translated 'mounting-places' — ⲙⲁ-ⲛ-ⲧⲁⲗⲟ from ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'to mount, ride.' Preserves the chariot imagery: the four sections of the holy Church are the four mounting-stations of the cosmic chariot. The verb ⲧⲉⲗⲟ ⲁⲣⲁⲩ in line 19-20 ('he mounted upon them') confirms the same root.

Translated 'pure sisters.' The qualitative ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲁⲓ̈ⲧ shows the feminine plural ending, and Manichaean four-fold ecclesiology requires this slot to be the Electae (female elect), paralleling the male Electi in segment 15, the male catechumens in segment 16-17, and the female catechumenae (ⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲏ, fem.) in segment 17-18.
Parsed as ⲧⲟⲩⲛ-ⲁⲛϩ 'raise to life' (causative of ⲱⲛϩ 'live'). Preserves the soteriological 'raising' direction per ⲧⲟⲩⲱ guidance.
Lycopolitan ⲃⲣⲟ = Sahidic ϫⲣⲟ 'victory.' ϯ ⲡⲃⲣⲟ = 'give the victory.'
Translated 'he himself' — the intensive/reflexive pronoun (= Lyc. ⲍⲱⲱϩ in vocabulary). Marks the Apostle as agent of his own decisive judicial act.

Parsed as ⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ 'know' (Lyc. = ⲥⲟⲟⲩⲛ), with the verb-stem split orthographically across the line break (ⲥⲛ̄ | ⲟⲩⲱⲛ → ⲥⲛⲟⲩⲛ/ⲥⲟⲩⲛ). 'The one who shall know the mysteries' is the recipient to whom the Apostle hands over the kingdom — a Manichaean topos for the gnostic-elect heir.
Preserved as a section-marker symbol. Likely an ornamental phi or paragraphos delimiting the chapter heading.

Greek χαῖρε/χαρά. In context (paired with ⲉⲓⲣⲏⲛⲏ 'peace' and connected with ἀσπασμός 'salutation'), this is the formal greeting/salutation 'rejoice.' Translating 'greeting' to preserve the greeting-formula sense rather than abstract 'joy.'
